To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the observability of a network can be derived from that of a network representation (e.g., NID); (2) the observability problem can be solved by selecting a minimal set of output nodes; and (3) the presence of graph symmetry can be taken into account to select the minimal output set.
(i) the observability of a network can be determined from the observability of its NID; and (ii) observability can be achieved with a minimal set of nodes and edges, in the presence of symmetries

1) the NEID can be derived from a NID, 2) observability of the NEID implies observability of the underlying NID, and 3) observability of a NEID can be achieved by selecting a minimal set of nodes that are not equivalent with respect to a given graph symmetry
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of identifying the minimum set of outputs required to obtain observability of a complex network.
the problem of detecting nodes and connections in complex dynamical networks and with the role of graph symmetry in this context.
the problem of observability of complex networks, with a focus on the role of graph symmetry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, given the NID and the NEID of a dynamical network, and given the set of available outputs, the NEID can be obtained from the NID, and vice-versa.
the observability of a network is determined by its symmetries and by the number of outputs.
, for the class of graphs considered, the NID and the NEID have the same observability properties, which can be achieved by selecting a minimal set of nodes, which is the same for both networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NID is more informative than the NEID, but that the latter can always be obtained from the former.
the NID can be reconstructed from the NEID under general assumptions.
the NID and the NEID are two complementary tools to study the observability problem in complex dynamical networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
observability is not only a problem for the nodes, but also for the edges of the network.
observability of the network can be assessed by looking at the observability properties of its graph representation.
observability of a network is not a property of the graph, but depends on the dynamical system generating the graph.
